extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, solicitors, and inventors preparing patent agreements and precedents
extracted.subtask_description: Model contractual clauses and drafting guidance for patent-related transactions (assignments, licences, mortgages, working agreements, royalties, accounts and related procedures). Includes suggested wording, statutory notes, and practical drafting provisos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignor's warranty of clear title
rubrics_metrics.description: Covenant that the assignor has not done, knowingly suffered, been party or privy to anything whereby the assigned premises or any part thereof are or may be impeached, affected, or incumbered in title, estate, or otherwise, or whereby he is prevented or hindered from joining in these presents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft as an express covenant from the assignor to the assignee to warrant clear title; use standard conveyancing language to protect assignee from prior acts affecting title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royalty payment schedule (by engine and shaft depth)
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee (W.) shall pay to B. and C., for every engine made or constructed under the patent, specified sums by way of royalty: e.g., £100 for engines winding from shafts not more than 100 yards depth; for shafts over 100 yards, 20s. for every yard of depth; different rates where balance rope is used (e.g., £50 for ≤100 yards, 10s. per yard for >100 yards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify precise measurement basis (from landing stage to loading stage), different rates for variants (e.g., balance rope), and explicit per-unit or per-yard calculations so royalties are unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special reduced royalties for initial orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision that for the first four orders obtained by W. a reduction shall be made: first engine (however large) £40 only; second engine one-quarter only of the standard royalty; third and fourth engines three-fourths only of the standard royalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit carve-outs for initial units (incentives) and state how reductions interact with standard royalty schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of royalties among multiple parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Division clause specifying shares: one-sixth of the royalties on all except the first four orders shall be paid to a named party; the whole of the royalties on each of the first four orders, and five-sixths of such royalties on remaining orders, to be handed over to B. and C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State fractions or percentages clearly and indicate treatment of special orders (first N orders) separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to procure foreign patents and pay duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Clause that W. shall use his best endeavours to take out the letters patent in India, Canada, and South Australia respectively, and pay all necessary and proper stamp duties requisite for keeping up the same, and do all in his power to further introduction and sale of engines in those limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If territorial protection required, obligate the licensee/assignee to prosecute foreign filings and maintain registrations, with responsibility for associated costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounts and recordkeeping of manufactured articles and licences
rubrics_metrics.description: W. will enter into books the particulars of all engines made in his district under the patent, particulars of all licences granted, consideration paid or reserved, names and addresses of grantees, and make plain and perfect entries of every sum of money received in respect of such licence; produce vouchers; allow inspection by B. and C. or their agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require detailed books (including order and invoice books), vouchers, and inspection rights; spell out information to be recorded to enable verification of royalties and licence activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly accounting and royalty payment schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: During exclusive protection, W. shall render to B. and C., within one calendar month after specified quarterly days (25 March, 24 June, 29 September, 25 December), a just and true account of moneys, particulars of licences granted and articles manufactured during the quarter, and shall pay royalties as soon as engines are delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify fixed accounting dates and timelines for reconciliation and payments; tie royalty payments to delivery events where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduction of preliminary expenses from early royalties
rubrics_metrics.description: W. shall be at liberty to deduct the sum of £150 (amount paid to B. and C. for preliminary expenses) or the full royalties reserved upon the first three engines at the rate of £50, and the royalties upon such engine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit deduction clauses to recoup preliminary costs, with clear numeric limits and interaction with royalty schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration of disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: If any dispute arises touching these presents or their construction, the matter shall be referred to two arbitrators or their umpire pursuant to the Common Law Procedure Act, 1854, and the submission may be made a rule of the High Court of Justice without notice to any other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert arbitration clause specifying governing arbitration statute, number of arbitrators/umpire, and method to make award enforceable (e.g., make it a rule of court).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortgage of letters patent with proviso for redemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Mortgagor assigns invention and letters patent to mortgagee for residue of term, subject to proviso that if mortgagor pays the principal sum with interest on due day, the mortgagee shall reassign the invention and patents to mortgagor on request and at his cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit redemption provision (pay-and-reassign) and state costs for reassignment; reference to conveying statutes where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortgagor covenant to keep patent alive (pay stamp duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mortgagor covenants to pay all stamp duties payable by law for keeping up the letters patent for the full term (e.g., fourteen years) from the date and within the time prescribed for such payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the mortgagor responsible for statutory maintenance payments unless otherwise agreed; specify period and statutory timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortgagor's obligation to protect patent from infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Mortgagor will use his best endeavours to discover any infringement and will notify mortgagee; if required in writing by mortgagee, either initiate proceedings himself or, if mortgagee takes proceedings, assist to render them effectual, and will pay on demand the costs of the mortgagee relating thereto as between solicitor and client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require active monitoring and cooperation on enforcement; include cost liability and ability for mortgagee to step in and charge expenses to mortgagor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortgagee's power to pay expenses and charge mortgagor
rubrics_metrics.description: If mortgagor neglects to make payments, it shall be lawful for mortgagee to pay the same, and monies or expenses incurred by mortgagee shall be repaid by mortgagor on demand and charged upon the mortgaged premises with interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant mortgagee express power to advance funds to protect security and create charge for reimbursement with interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortgagor's power to grant licences pre-default (as mortgagee's attorney)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to mortgagee becoming entitled to exercise power of sale, mortgagor may, in the name and as attorney of mortgagee, grant licences for use of the invention and patents for such terms and conditions as he thinks fit, subject to limitations: cannot enter covenants in mortgagee's name, no exclusive licence without mortgagee's written consent, reserve best rent/royalty without taking fine or premium, include revocation power for mortgagee on breach or non-payment, require counterpart and covenant by licensee for payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow practical exploitation while protecting mortgagee's interests: limit scope of licences, require reservation of best terms, include revocation and counterpart requirements, obtain mortgagee consent for exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortgagee's power to grant licences post-entitlement (broad powers)
rubrics_metrics.description: After mortgagee is entitled to exercise power of sale, mortgagee (or his executors/assigns) may grant licences (exclusive or otherwise) for such term, conditions and consideration (gross sum, rents, royalties, or otherwise) as he may think fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once security matures, grant broad commercial discretion to mortgagee to monetize the patent; ensure consideration and licence terms are captured in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of sale conditions and required notice periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Mortgagee shall not exercise power of sale unless default has been made in payment of moneys secured and he has given notice in writing to mortgagor (or left/sent registered letter) to pay off the moneys owing, and default continues for specified calendar months; likewise interest arrears or default in covenants may trigger power of sale after specified notice periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify triggering events and concrete notice/arrear periods before exercising power of sale to ensure enforceability and to afford mortgagor opportunity to remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of purchasers at mortgage sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchaser at sale need not inquire into whether the default or notice conditions have occurred; sale is valid despite irregularities as regards regularity or necessity, and purchaser's remedy against irregularity is damages only; purchaser discharged by mortgagee's receipt for purchase money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft purchase-protection clauses to promote marketability of sale and protect buyers; limit recourse against purchasers to damages and provide purchaser discharge by receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust and priority in application of sale proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: Mortgagee shall hold moneys arising from sale and any gross sums/rents/royalties received upon licences upon trust: first to reimburse costs and expenses of sale and administration; next to apply moneys toward satisfaction of monies owing on the security; then to pay surplus to mortgagor, his heirs or assigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State order of application of proceeds clearly (costs first, debt second, surplus to mortgagor) and require mortgagee accounting to mortgagor for surplus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of sale may be exercised by person entitled to mortgage money
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of sale may be exercised by any person or persons entitled to receive and give a discharge for moneys owing on the security; mortgagee may exercise through those entitled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow flexibility in who may exercise power of sale (holders of the security), but ensure authority is documented when exercised by assignees/holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indemnity / non-liability for involuntary losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Mortgagee, his heirs, executors, administrators, or assigns shall not be answerable for any involuntary losses which may happen in or about the exercise or execution of any of the powers or trusts herein contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include indemnity/non-liability language to protect mortgagee acting in good faith from accidental or involuntary losses arising from execution of powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement for working a patent — financier advances all required monies
rubrics_metrics.description: In working agreement the capitalist (C.D.) shall advance and contribute from time to time all moneys necessary for working the patent, and may include costs of protecting/defending the same and expenses of obtaining renewals/extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate responsibility for capital and enforcement costs explicitly; consider registering such partnership-like agreements at the Patent Office (note in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital contributions considered joint property in equal shares
rubrics_metrics.description: All moneys advanced by capitalist shall be considered to be the property of both parties in equal proportions; no money required to be advanced by inventor in consideration of the value of invention and his services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out treatment of advances as joint capital and avoid implying inventor must outlay cash where contribution is considered satisfied by his services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of net profits equally
rubrics_metrics.description: Net profits derived from working the patent shall be equally divided between the parties in equal shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify profit-sharing ratio and how 'net profits' are calculated if necessary (deductions, accounting standards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee's duty to work the patent and maintain accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent shall be worked and the business carried on in the name of the patentee; proper accounts to be kept of payments made, moneys received, liabilities incurred, and transactions; all moneys received shall be paid into a joint bank account and only drawn on joint cheque of both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require working in patentee's name, strict bookkeeping, joint bank control and joint cheque disbursements to ensure transparency and joint control of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custody of books with access and periodic accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Books of account and documents relating to the patent shall be kept in custody of A.B. (patentee), but C.D. shall at all times have access; accounts shall be made up half yearly with first account date specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide access rights to financier and prescribe periodic accounting intervals; locate custody but preserve inspection rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and termination by notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrangement remains in force until expiration of patent term (and renewals) so long as both parties live, but subject to right to determine the agreement at the expiration of specified years by giving 3 calendar months' previous notice in writing to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define default duration (patent term) and contractual termination rights including notice period and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination on death — survivor's option to purchase deceased's share
rubrics_metrics.description: If arrangement determined by death, survivor has the option to purchase the deceased's share by paying representatives the deceased's share of capital and unpaid profits within specified months after death (or by instalments as provided); upon exercise assignments and acts to vest title in survivor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear timing windows for exercising option, payment terms (lump sum or instalments), interest on unpaid sums, and mechanics of vesting/assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: If option not exercised — joint ownership and rights to work
rubrics_metrics.description: If survivor does not exercise option, letters patent and royalties shall belong to survivor and deceased's representatives jointly, and both parties shall be entitled to work and use the invention and grant non-exclusive licences without accounting to the other for resulting profits/royalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify ownership and exploitation rights where purchase option lapses; define limitation to non-exclusive licences and accountings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment by one party
rubrics_metrics.description: If one party desires to abandon working the patent while the other wishes to continue, the abandoning party may give notice in writing and the arrangement shall cease; the abandoning party shall be under no further liability in respect of expenses and the patent and profits shall thenceforth be absolute property of the continuing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mechanism for unilateral abandonment with notice, effect on liabilities, and transfer of rights to continuing party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement variant — equal moiety advances and recovery of excess advances
rubrics_metrics.description: Where each party advances one moiety of moneys required, if either advances in excess of his bound share he shall be entitled to recover a moiety of such excess from the other with interest, and such moiety and interest shall be a charge upon the other's share and interest in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When parties share financing equally, provide remedy for unequal advances including interest and security (charge) on the other's interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of assignment of copyright in a design (elements required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form: assignor transfers right in registered design No. __ in class __ to assignee and authorizes assignee to insert his name on register of designs accordingly; option to insert limitations of rights if desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prescribed form language for assignment; authorize registration office entry; include optional limitations if partial assignment intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of a trade mark should include goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: Form: assignor, being registered proprietor of trade mark No. __ in class __, in consideration of £__, hereby assigns the trade mark to assignee together with the goodwill of the business concerned in the goods with respect to which the trade mark is registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning a trade mark, expressly include transfer of associated goodwill to preserve statutory requirements; identify the mark sufficiently and recite consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting note — omit obsolete or unnecessary words per Conveyancing Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenthetical note stating certain words (e.g., 'his executors, administrators, and assigns') are now unnecessary in a covenant by virtue of Conveyancing Act, 1881, ss. 59, 60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting modern deeds, check relevant statutes to avoid redundant phrasing; include statutory citations as drafting notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration recommendation for working agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that an agreement which practically constitutes a partnership for working a patent ought to be registered at the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where agreements affect patent ownership/working in a partnership-like manner, register with the Patent Office to ensure public record and enforceability.
